d: What swerve gives the application: its log, the cache and the messages shared by every worker (see the methods), and the state of the worker.
The log of this process: swerve's own, in its format (the time, this worker's slot), wherever swerve logs (the terminal, or --log's file); a NullLogger with -q.
Send a message to every subscriber of $topic, in every worker process of this swerve, this one included.
Receive what is published to $topic from now on: foreach (Swerve::subscribe('chat') as $message) { ...
The cache every worker shares, held by the master: see Cache.
A handle on the name $name, one holder at a time across the workers; claims nothing until acquire() is called: `Swerve::claim('name')->acquire()` is null, or the held handle.
Whether this worker drains: it is shutting down, reloading or being recycled, and finishes the requests in flight.
The installed version, as Composer knows it: 0.1.0-alpha3, or dev-main in a checkout.
Messages published to a topic, from Swerve::subscribe(): iterate over it to receive them.
The messages, as they come; null after each $heartbeat seconds without one.
A handle on a name that one holder at a time can hold across the whole server, from Swerve::claim().
Whether nobody holds the name now; nothing is claimed.
Take the name, trying every 20 ms for up to $timeout seconds when another holds it: whoever tries first when it frees gets it, in no order.
Whether this handle holds the name.
Give the claim up, so that another can take it.
Releases: synchronous, so it cannot suspend.

A topic where every subscriber, in every worker, receives the messages in one and the same order, and each publisher's own messages keep theirs: $ledger = new OrderedChannel('ledger'); $ledger->write(['debit', 12]); foreach ($ledger as $entry) { ...
Append $message, as Swerve::publish() sends one: nothing is written, and the message is dropped, while the channel has no subscriber anywhere.
Receive what is written from now on, as Swerve::subscribe() does: the subscription exists once this returns.
Subscribes with the defaults, so `foreach ($channel as $message)` subscribes at the foreach.
A subscription fell further behind its topic than its maxLag, see Subscription.
A WebSocket connection (RFC 6455), server side.

The next text or binary message, or null once the connection is closed: by the client, by close(), because the client broke the protocol, or because swerve drains (a shutdown or reload), which closes it with 1001.
The messages received, until the connection closes.
Whether the message receive() returned last was binary, rather than text.
Send a text message, which must be UTF-8; nothing once the connection is closed.
Send a binary message; nothing once the connection is closed.
Say goodbye, once: receive() returns null from then on, and the connection closes after the client's own goodbye, or a moment without one.
This class defines the essential API for all coroutine based applications.
Register a coroutine/Fiber to run in the event loop and await the result.
Creates a normal coroutine and starts running it.
Launches a service coroutine independently of the context scope.
Wait for a coroutine, a promise, or a SelectableInterface to complete and return the result.
Schedule a closure to run when the current coroutine completes, or, when called inside `phasync::withContext()`, as that call returns, whichever comes first.
Cancel a coroutine, or every coroutine of a context.
Interrupt the wait of a suspended coroutine with an exception, once.
Yield time so that other coroutines can continue processing.
Suspend the fiber until immediately after some other fibers has performed work.
Suspend the coroutine until the stream can be read without blocking: data arrived, the peer finished, or the stream failed.
Suspend the coroutine until the stream can be written without blocking, as `phasync::readable()` does for reading.
Creates a channel pair which can be used to communicate between multiple coroutines.
A publisher works like channels, but supports many subscribing coroutines concurrently.
Signal all coroutines that are waiting for an event represented by the object $signal to resume.
Pause execution of the current coroutine until an event is signalled represented by the object $signal.
Wait until every coroutine of $context, and of the contexts nested in it, has ended; a server that lets requests start coroutines of their own waits for them this way before it exits.
Returns true when called from within a coroutine context.

Run $fn in the current coroutine as if it were the main coroutine of a phasync::run() of $context, without starting a coroutine, which costs far more: it returns what $fn returns, once the coroutines $fn started in the context have ended too.
The event loop, for code that waits with its low-level API (`EventLoop::park()`).
Get the currently running coroutine.
The root context of the running coroutine: its request, so to say.
The context of the running coroutine: the object given to run(), go() or withContext(), or the one it inherited.
A readable channel provides messages asynchronously from various sources.
This function can be used to activate the channel so that the deadlock protection does not fail.
Closes the channel.
True if the channel is no longer readable.
Returns the next item that can be read.
Returns true if the channel is still readable.
This function can be used to activate the channel so that the deadlock protection does not fail.
Closes the channel.
True if the channel is no longer writable.
Write a value to the channel.
Returns true if the channel is still readable.
The operation that was being awaited has been cancelled.
This class provides an efficient tool for waiting until multiple coroutines have completed their task.
Add work to the WaitGroup, like Go's WaitGroup.Add(delta).
Signal that work has been completed to the WaitGroup.
Wait until the WaitGroup has signalled that all work is done.
This function was renamed to `WaitGroup::await()` to harmonize with the SelectableInterface API.
This class provides an efficient tool for limiting the rate at which events happen, potentially across coroutines.
Blocks the current coroutine if rate limiting is needed.
Launches and manages a child process on POSIX and Windows alike.
Launch a new process.
Returns true if the process is still running.
Returns true if the process is stopped (generally via `Process::sigstop()`).
Return the exitcode of the process, or false if the process is still running.
Send a POSIX signal to the process.
SIGTERM requests a process to terminate.
This signal forces a process to terminate immediately.
This signal is typically sent when the user types the interrupt character (usually Ctrl+C).
This signal pauses a process's execution.
SIGCONT is used to resume a process previously stopped by SIGSTOP or another stop signal.
Originally sent when a terminal was closed, today SIGHUP is often used to instruct background processes to reload their configuration files or to gracefully restart.
Perform a Fiber-blocking read from the given process pipe.
Perform a Fiber-blocking write to the given process pipe.
An asynchronous PSR-18 HTTP client, in the package phasync/http-client.
Pass values between coroutines with phasync::channel(): a read waits for a writer, a write into a full channel waits for a reader.
